title: fix(update): inspect collected legacy service handoffs
body:
## Problem

Full Release Validation's published-driver compatibility lane for `2026.9.3 → candidate` deterministically refused candidate validation with `managed-service-preflight`.

The shipped 2026.9.2/2026.9.3 updater handoff predates `serviceManagerUid`. After that updater stops a Linux native service, systemd may collect the unit before the candidate reinspects it. Candidate validation then lacks the manager boundary needed to load the collected unit and treats the managed service as unavailable.

## Solution

For a verified Linux handoff that is already stopped, has a captured service environment, and omits the newer manager UID, retain the running installed updater account as the native manager boundary. Explicit recorded manager identity continues to take precedence.

This is limited to legacy stopped handoffs under the existing current-authority assertion.

## Evidence

- New regression: collected systemd unit from a shipped stopped handoff retains the installed updater's manager UID.
- Identity suite: 4/4 passed; 24.6s cold invocation, new test 9ms.
- Service-maintenance siblings: 42/42 passed.
- Service-fingerprint siblings: 30/30 passed.
- Core production typecheck passed.
- The simulated Linux effective UID is installed and restored portably for Windows test hosts.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- AutoReview P0/P1: scoped clean.

FRV source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37502933059

- Exact hosted published-driver proof: [CI run 37513855606, job 112445769676](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37513855606/job/112445769676) passed the immutable candidate artifact from exact head `d0f62baf965bd63f05a12e6ac41e0959753e6659` through the shipped `openclaw@latest` stable driver (`2026.9.8`). The update finished with readiness 200 and verified the running candidate version; the only unrelated run failure was the inherited MCP dependency audit.
